name: PROVIDERS
summary: Which account each box is signed in as, how much of its limit is spent, and when a parked one frees up again.

surface.hint: accounts across your boxes: usage, and when a parked one comes back

run._note: One bound root, not a config flag plus a store flag. fleet.json is the DECLARED fleet and samples.jsonl is what we have read from it; splitting them lets the two disagree about which fleet you are looking at.

provider._note: No companion. Sampling costs a real API call against the very budget it reports, so it never runs on a timer — a background poller would be an instrument that quietly consumes what it measures. The caller asks.

_roots_note: A NEW KIND, and it had to be. The fleet list is box-level — one box has many projects and one fleet — so project/media/canvas/footage are all wrong, and the runtime state dir is disposable while this config is AUTHORED. Declaring it surfaced that the root-kind vocabulary was a closed hardcoded set of four in the SDK; it is open now (studio.json roots{}), pinned by test/root-kinds.test.mjs.
_verbs_note: Two verbs with deliberately different costs. /api/fleet/state is free and is what the surface polls, so opening the dashboard spends nothing. /api/fleet/sample spends one real request per box and is only ever reached by an explicit click.

requires._binaries_note: The controller reaches IN. Boxes have one-way ACLs and cannot initiate back, so a pull is the only shape that works — and it is also what keeps the credential on the box instead of here. ssh targets are the operator's existing ones; this app deliberately manages no hosts file, no keys and no tunnels. If ssh to a declared name does not already work, that is a provisioning fact to report, not something a dashboard should paper over.
